text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Some ruling party members of parliament demanded the creation of a parliamentary committee to scrutinise the pyramid schemes.
- The ruling party has not accepted a referendum proposed by a monarchist party on the country's way of governing.
- A mining trade union asks President Sali Berisha to interfere and disallow the privatisation of the chromium industry.
- The appreciation of hard currencies on the free market shows that the inflow of leks into pyramid schemes has come to a halt.
- Prices of vegetables and other food products rose significantly over the last week.
- Tirana's new mayor Albert Brojka promises non-stop water and power supply for the capital next year.
- A prosecutor demanded a total of 178 years jail for nine senior ex-communist officials charged of crimes against humanity.
- Some 300 tonnes of old pesticides in the central city of Elbasan will be destroyed.
- One of Albania's biggest ships, Tirana, has been stuck for eight months in a Turkish port because of a clash with the Orion transport company.
- Police arrest another person in connection with the recently-discovered band alleged to have committed several crimes over the last four years.
- The polio outbreak claims the life of a 14-year old.
- The Privatisation Ministry plans to speed up the privatisation process in the key sectors of oil, gas, mineral resources, public services and banks.
